summary: Defines a PPP Link Control Protocol option that lets peers negotiate the language and character set used in messages. It updates RFC 1570, RFC 1994 and RFC 2284. It is a proposed standard.

eli5.summary: It lets two computers on a direct link agree on what language to use for messages meant for people, like saying which language to speak.

questions: what is the ppp lcp internationalization option
what is the default charset for ppp messages
subtitle: A PPP option that lets two peers agree on the language and character set for human-readable messages.

tldr.problem: LCP and authentication packets in PPP may contain text meant for people, but there was no way to negotiate which language and charset that text uses, as RFC 2277 requires.
tldr.mechanism: A new LCP configuration option, type 28, carries a four-octet MIBenum charset value and an ASCII language tag.
tldr.outcome: If the peer rejects the option, the default language and charset must be used. The RFC updates RFC 1570, RFC 1994 and RFC 2284.

today: RFC 2484 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 1570, RFC 1994 and RFC 2284. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why a Language Option
sections.content:
The Point-to-Point Protocol (RFC 1661) has an extensible Link Control Protocol (LCP), which can also negotiate an authentication protocol. Both LCP and authentication packets may contain human-readable text.

This RFC defines an LCP configuration option for negotiating the character set and language, as required by RFC 2277. It updates RFC 2284, RFC 1994 and RFC 1570.
sections.eli5: Sometimes the computers send notes meant for people. This option lets them agree on which language the notes use.

sections.title: Negotiation Rules
sections.content:
The option uses LCP Option Type value 28, named Internationalization. It MAY be negotiated independently in each direction. An implementation SHOULD send only one instance of the option, giving its preferred language and charset.

If the peer rejects the option, the default language and charset MUST be used for all human-readable messages sent to that peer.
sections.eli5: Each side says which language it likes. If the other side says no thanks, both use the standard one.

sections.title: The Option Format
sections.content:
The option has a Type of 28, a Length of at least 7, a four-octet MIBenum field and a variable Language-Tag.

MIBenum identifies a charset and MUST be one in the IANA charset registry. The default is UTF-8, whose MIBenum value is 106. The Language-Tag is an ASCII string as defined in RFC 1766. Tags are case-insensitive in principle, but implementations SHOULD send only lower-case tags. The default tag is i-default.
sections.eli5: The label has a number for the alphabet and a short word for the language.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC's only security note is that an attacker might manipulate the option so that displayable messages become unintelligible to the reader.
sections.eli5: A trickster could change the language setting so the notes are impossible to read.

fields.name: Language-Tag
fields.desc: ASCII language tag, variable length; default i-default.
